choices.text:
The bug is on line 5: `strncat` stops at the first NUL byte in `tok`, so if the token contains an embedded NUL, only the prefix before the NUL is copied — the reconstructed SQL token is silently truncated, and the rest of the token (which may contain attacker-controlled SQL) is dropped. Additionally, `strncat` doesn't respect `sql_cap` bounds, but the primary issue given the stated assumptions is the embedded-NUL truncation.

Answer: 5
